title: How the Proud Tek Team Is Organised
summary: Proud Tek runs every account through three functions — international sales engineering, RF / production engineering and quality control — with a fourth, supply chain and export, behind them. This page covers what each function owns, how an engineering escalation actually runs for a buyer programme, and the response times we hold ourselves to. Like our sister brand RFIDAK, we describe the functions rather than name individuals: the function is what a procurement team can hold us to, and it does not change when a person changes jobs. The editorial functions that sign off the guides on this site are on /about/review-board/.

sections.title: The functions and what they own
sections.intro: Proud Tek is a flat, engineering-first organisation. Each function is accountable end-to-end for the part of your programme it owns — from inquiry through dispatch — so buyer programmes are not handed across silos that lose context between steps. Production itself runs on contracted partner lines to our specification; the functions below are the people who write that specification and sign off the result.

features.title: International sales engineering
features.text: Your first reply, within 2–4 hours in Shenzhen business hours. Turns 'it depends' into a price, an MOQ and a lead time — a written quote within 24–48 hours — and keeps the thread moving across time zones. The same account engineer stays with a programme through reorders. English and Chinese as standard; Spanish and Arabic on assignment.

features.title: RF / production engineering
features.text: Owns the product and antenna specification and matches chip families and antenna designs to your installed readers or locks before production starts. Writes the encoding specification the partner lines execute, approves the first article and stays on the programme from pilot to year-three reorder so process context is never lost.

features.title: Quality control
features.text: Reads every incoming chip batch at the reel, runs 100% read/write, print, dimension and packaging inspection on every production batch and signs it off before release. Reports separately from scheduling — a lot that fails inspection is not shipped because of a date. Records retained seven years under the ISO 9001 system.

features.title: Supply chain and export
features.text: Owns chip allocation through authorised distribution, the forward stock buffer on critical SKUs, partner-line capacity reservations, freight and distributor safety stock — so availability and lead time sit with someone accountable, not a broker in the middle.

features.title: Editorial and review functions
features.text: The editorial team and the RF / production engineering function sign off the technical content on this site, separately from sales, with a public corrections log. See /about/review-board/.

sections.title: How engineering escalation actually works
sections.intro: Most buyer trust is won or lost during the first real engineering escalation — a reader-side error log, an anti-collision failure, a chip-specific encoding mismatch. The path below is how a typical issue moves from buyer's QA team to a corrected shipment.

items.label: Step 1 — Buyer signals the issue
items.text: Account engineer receives the issue (email, WhatsApp, support ticket) with the error context: reader make/model, firmware version, encoding sample, environmental conditions. We respond within 2-4 hours in Shenzhen business hours (Mon-Fri, GMT+8) with an initial assessment.

items.label: Step 2 — Engineering replay
items.text: RF / production engineering pulls the original encoding lot, replays the encoding scheme on a representative reader in our Shenzhen lab, and reproduces the issue if reader-side. The test fleet covers the major reader brands (Impinj, Zebra, Honeywell, Feig, ACR, Chainway, Bluebird).

items.label: Step 3 — Root cause and corrective action
items.text: Findings reported back to the buyer with the root cause, the corrective action (chip substitution, encoding scheme adjustment, lamination tuning, etc.) and the impact on remaining inventory. Buyer signs off on the proposed correction.

items.label: Step 4 — Remediation and prevention
items.text: Corrected batch produced on the partner line to the revised specification, or the screened-out lot replaced under our quality commitment. Corrective action filed in the ISO 9001 corrective-action register; future production travelers updated to prevent recurrence.

sections.title: How we operate — the principles behind the team
sections.intro: Proud Tek is deliberately a flat, engineering-first organisation. A handful of operating principles explain most of how the team behaves on a buyer program — and why the same call gets made whether or not anyone is watching.

features.title: Engineering-first, flat org
features.text: Decisions sit with the engineer closest to the specification and the partner line, not a management layer removed from the work — fewer hand-offs, faster technical answers.

features.title: One owner per programme
features.text: The account engineer who scopes your deal runs it for its life — RFQ, samples, pilot, production and reorder — instead of handing off to junior sales who do not know the chip-side trade-offs.

features.title: Quality independent of the ship date
features.text: Quality control reports separately from production scheduling and cannot be overridden by ship-date pressure. A lot that fails the 100% read test is not released.

features.title: Manufacturer-direct accountability
features.text: Operating since 2008 — you deal with the team that owns the specification, the chip sourcing and the QC sign-off, not a trading layer. Tooling and production run on contracted partner lines to that specification; when something goes wrong there is an accountable function, not a supplier to point at.

features.title: Editorial integrity, audited
features.text: Published guides are reviewed by the engineering function and corrections are logged publicly, because procurement teams check. See the review functions and the corrections log.

features.title: Predictable response
features.text: First reply within 2–4 hours in Shenzhen business hours (Mon–Fri, GMT+8); written quotes within 24–48 hours, valid 30 days. Predictable timing over promised speed.

sections.title: How buyer programs get staffed
sections.intro: Program staffing follows a simple rule: the person who scopes the deal is the person who runs it for the life of the program. This is not aspirational — it is how the organization is structured.

before: Sales engineer scopes the deal, then hands off to a junior account manager who does not understand the chip-side trade-offs.
Account contact rotates every 12-18 months as headcount churns at the supplier.
Engineering escalation requires re-explaining the program context every time.
Reorders fall back to 'standard pricing' that ignores the negotiated terms of the original deal.
Quality issues bounce between sales and QA without a clear owner.
after: Same account engineer from initial RFQ through year-three reorder — they own the program.
Account engineers are Proud Tek team members, not contract sales staff.
Engineering escalation routes straight to the RF / production engineering function that wrote the specification — no re-explanation of context needed.
Reorders inherit the original commercial terms and engineering scope by default.
Quality issues have a documented owner (account engineer + quality control) with a response time commitment.

sections.title: Buyer support hours and response SLA
sections.intro: Predictable response timing matters more than promised speed. The SLA below is what we actually meet on qualified B2B inquiries, not a marketing target.
bullets: First reply — within 2–4 hours during Shenzhen business hours (Mon–Fri, 09:00–19:00 GMT+8); written quotes within 24–48 hours.
Urgent escalations — same business day during Shenzhen working hours.
After-hours coverage — email and WhatsApp monitored outside business hours; non-urgent items queued for the next business morning.
Time-zone overlap — Asia-Pacific buyers get same-day; Europe buyers get same-day for issues raised before 14:00 GMT+8; Americas buyers get a next-morning reply.
Holiday schedule — published in advance for Chinese New Year, National Day and other major holidays; safety stock and pre-orders accommodate holiday lead-time gaps.

callout.label: After-hours and named-engineer coverage
callout.text: If your organization needs 24/7 support coverage for a critical-path program (e.g., live event RFID, hotel-lock retrofit during peak season), say so on the initial inquiry. We can structure a named-engineer arrangement with after-hours availability as part of an annual-volume agreement.

faq.question: Who actually picks up the phone if I email Proud Tek?
faq.answer: Account engineers respond to inbound inquiries within 2-4 hours in Shenzhen business hours (Mon-Fri, GMT+8). For new inquiries, the engineer assigned to your geography and product family takes the conversation. For existing programs, the engineer who scoped the original deal continues to own the relationship — including reorders, escalations and engineering follow-up.

faq.question: Is the engineering team in China or distributed?
faq.answer: Sales engineering, RF / production engineering, quality control and supply-chain staff are based in Shenzhen; we have no overseas offices. Production runs on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our specification. Language coverage is English / Chinese as standard, with Spanish and Arabic by assignment; time-zone overlap with European and American customers is managed through scheduled response windows.

faq.question: Who is accountable if my programme has a problem?
faq.answer: The account engineer who scoped the programme and the quality-control function that signed off the batch — a documented pair for every order. Engineering escalations go to the RF / production engineering function that wrote the specification, which replays the issue in our Shenzhen lab and corrects the specification before the partner line re-runs the batch. We do not subcontract account management to short-tenure contract sales staff.

faq.question: What is the corrections process for technical content on the site?
faq.answer: Any reader can report a factual error in a published guide via the corrections channel (see /about/corrections/). Reported issues are reviewed by the editorial team and the RF / production engineering function within five business days; substantive corrections are logged publicly with date, change and reason. We do not silently edit content to hide outdated claims.

faq.question: Do you disclose affiliate or supplier relationships in your guides?
faq.answer: Yes. The disclosures page (/about/disclosures/) lists current supplier, partnership and affiliate relationships that could influence the recommendation in a guide. Per-page disclosures appear at the end of any article where the relationship is relevant. We treat editorial integrity as a procurement-team trust signal, not a legal afterthought.
